title: Frontiers: The Impact of Ad-Blockers on Online Consumer Behavior
eligible_reason: Design qualifies. Panelists adopt ad-blockers at individual-specific weeks, and Model 1 of each spending table is areg y L1.adblocker_installed i.week_id, absorb(panel_id) with no controls (user FE + week FE, binary staggered treatment, never-adopters as controls). The paper is not eligible because the package ships no data: dataset.dta is referenced but absent.
design_notes: impact_of_adblockers.do: five OLS outcomes (log total online spending; heavy-advertiser, light-advertiser, new-brand and not-new-brand spending), each with Models 1-3 (Model 1 no controls; Model 2 + holidays; Model 3 + holidays + demographic bins), all areg absorb(panel_id) with i.week_id and vce(robust). Two count outcomes (search-engine and e-commerce visits) use xtpoisson fe. A 'Parallel Trends' block adds c.week_id and c.week_id#adopter trends on pre-adoption observations (falsification, not eligible). The README lists the dataset variables, but the data are not included.
n_eligible_specs_note: Model 1 (no controls) of each of the five log-spending outcomes. Models 2-3 (holidays control) and the Poisson columns are excluded. Counts are design-level, since no data are shipped.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Cannot be computed (data not shipped). By construction, adoption weeks vary by panelist.

specs.treatment_definition: Binary indicator that the panelist has an ad-blocker installed, lagged one week (xtset panel_id week_id). Adoption weeks vary by panelist; adblocker_adopter = max(adblocker_installed) marks ever-adopters, so non-adopters serve as never-treated controls.
specs.reported_location: Table (spending), Model 1 (exact table number unknown; no article text)
specs.notes: Model 2 adds c.holidays (paid holidays in the panelist's location-week, time-varying) and Model 3 adds holidays plus i.income_bin i.education_bin i.age_bin i.household_size; both are ineligible. Need to check whether adblocker_installed ever switches off (uninstalls).
